- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to correct for momentum decay.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check sentiment for recent negative spikes — if present, model may be overconfident; apply downward bias.  
- If true outcome is significantly above forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check sentiment for recent positive spikes — if present, model may be underestimating bullish momentum; apply upward bias.  
- Model often overestimates in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing or lag correction for first 3–5 forecast points.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 2–3 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), model tends to err on the side of overestimation; apply conservative correction (−1–2%).
